answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in a tundra agent mesh, nodes authenticate peers via seismic ground-wave ranging. Each agent drives an onyx penetrator using a motorized quill actuator into permafrost, emitting acoustic pulses verified by neighboring geophones. An adversary cannot virtualize identities on one host because each requires dedicated mechanical actuators and physical ground contact. However, seasonal permafrost thaw attenuates acoustic propagation, causing false authentication rejections.
